methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the focus was on the functional description of the D flip-flop. For the generated technical specification, the analysis considered both the combinational logic and the timing logic aspects, extracting atomic units from each.
mindtraced_atomic_units: q updates to d on positive edge of clk
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module with inputs clk, d, ar and output q
When ar is asserted, q is forced to 0
When ar is de-asserted, q potentially updates with d on rising edge of clk (combinational view)
Combinational logic can be viewed as a multiplexer controlled by ar
Critical path is from ar to q
q asynchronously resets to 0 when ar is asserted high
q updates to the value of d on the rising edge of clk when ar is deasserted low
always block triggered by positive edge of clk or positive edge of ar
Non-blocking assignment used to update q
When ar is high, q is set to 0
Otherwise, q is updated with the value of d on the rising edge of clk
